positions.as_written: Assess rotation near extension and record the grade, accepting its modest reliability.
Measure slope and plateau morphology where rotatory laxity is prominent.
Treat rotatory laxity as a combined motion rather than a single measurement.
Treat rotational control as the outcome that decides whether a pivoting athlete is satisfied, and as the one the evidence base measures least well.
Consider lateral augmentation by rotational demand and laxity grade rather than by translation.
Repair the lateral posterior horn where it is torn, on rotational grounds.
Measure slope in a pivoting athlete, particularly before revision.
